synopsis: The corpus uses arXiv research across operational-domain definition, braking logic, synthetic data and simulation credibility, but publication status and applicability limit its authority: the November 2025 agricultural ODD framework is academic work rather than a standard, the 2025 crash-reconstruction braking study was not peer-reviewed, and the 2020 validation review has unclear peer-review status [f1399, f1400, f6347, f7666]. The agricultural framework borrows ISO 34503 concepts from road vehicles and reviews EMESRT PR-5A as an off-road ODD approach [f1399, f6713]. On-road braking examples include a 2023 staged warning/partial/full-braking study assuming 2.5 seconds of driver reaction time and a 2025 time-to-brake approach with activation gates intended to suppress false positives [f6186, f6187]. For simulation inputs, the corpus cites a vendor-co-authored lidar dust model compared against experiments in 2021 and LiDARDustX, covering mines and quarries, published on 28 May 2025; Duc et al.'s May 2025 on-road study found measurable real–synthetic point-cloud gaps and useful performance with a 50/50 mixture, explicitly not a transferable optimum [f6380, f7064, f7073, f7074, f7075]. The 2020 review describes CSAU and EMDAP as emphasizing scaling to address missing data while criticizing their implicit treatment of subjective evidence as a transparency weakness [f7666, f7667].

relations.note: Clarifies that the proposed agricultural framework is academic work, not a standard.
Adds the framework's review of EMESRT PR-5A as an off-road ODD approach.
Details activation logic and false-positive suppression in the 2025 crash-reconstruction study.
Adds transparency criticisms to the same review's account of scaling-based validation approaches.
Adds a useful real–synthetic mixture result to the study's domain-gap findings.
Limits the 50/50 result to its study context rather than a general optimum.
Measured domain gaps support caution about transferring mixture proportions to other settings.
